notes: A100 microbenchmark cycles and random-access observations lack a formal product subject and complete conditions. They are not GA100 facts.
Full-design component counts, SM structure, and one per-SM dense FP16 FMA path are staged. Array shape and many implementation limits remain gaps.
A completed field-specific local search found no standalone GA100 bare-die public price. A100 card/module prices and qualitative cost language are different objects or non-price statements.

The v2 reverse-removal draft selects seven sources, including ISSCC for independent LR-PHY and conflict evidence. Nineteen stable payload copies, formal application, Windows hard gates, and independent signature remain outstanding.
Name, family, type, vendor, and architecture relation are staged. Status, availability, release, positioning, and administrative cutoff remain unresolved.

PCIe 4.0 x16 and the GA100-owned NVLink interface class are represented without assuming quantity. Architecture NVLink3 fault, remote-memory, and LR-PHY mechanisms are covered; count, lane/rate normalization, injection/aggregate bandwidth, absolute latency, and topology remain targeted gaps.

Covered: per-SM 262144-byte register file, four register-file groups, 196608-byte combined L1/shared memory, L2 identity, and architecture-projected L1/shared management/locality. Still unresolved or missing: usable and L2 capacity, read/write/bidirectional bandwidth, per-cycle transfers, seconds latency, banks, ports, granularity, read/write model, consistency, pooling, virtual memory, compression, and full-die aggregates.

Nine Tensor paths now have exact A/B/program-visible accumulation closure, including the FP16-to-FP16 variant. TF32 output is direct; every other product, physical-accumulation, output, rounding, scaling, saturation, subnormal, and sparsity cell has a path-specific fact or requirement.
Foundry, process, area, and transistor count are staged. Die count, clock, power, and HBM-interface total are unresolved. Package-related fields are not applicable.
GA100 DPO, row remapping, containment, detection, and recovery are staged with driver, HBM, application, and reset conditions.
Ampere split barriers and warp reduction are covered. Product CUDA Graph and MIG scheduling behavior are not promoted to full-GA100 facts.
CUDA 11.0 and PTX 7.x target documentation is staged. Product MIG behavior and CUDA Graph claims remain conditional or excluded.
OFA, video decode, sparse MMA, async copy, and warp reduction are covered. Each other template mechanism has its own evidence target and gap.
